name: IL-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Mike Quigley running with large cash advantage
Republican challenger underfunded with no visible campaign finance
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
model.rationale: Quigley holds a D+19 seat with over $1.1 million on hand against a challenger with no reported fundraising, and markets price this near-certain for Democrats. Fundamentals point to a margin in the mid-20s, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: Any late polling or surge in challenger fundraising would be the only signal that this race is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mike Quigley, a well-established Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in this Chicago-based district that leans heavily Democratic by about 19 points. He has raised over $725,000 and holds roughly $1.2 million in cash, while Republican Tommy Hanson reports no fundraising activity and draws no outside support. No independent polls of the race are available, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive.

Prediction markets give Democrats roughly a 97% chance of holding the seat, and the fundamentals point to a margin in the mid-20s. With no evidence of a serious Republican campaign infrastructure, the race is rated Safe Democratic, with modest residual uncertainty from the absence of polling.
